Metadata.title: Hyphae Consensus
Metadata.description: Hyphae Consensus portal: verifiable multi-agent reasoning and decision accountability.

App.name: Hyphae Consensus
App.tagline: Verifiable multi-agent reasoning and decision accountability
App.intro: Three AI roles (Proposer, Critic and Evidence Evaluator) work through a software-engineering problem. The runtime retrieves evidence from Hyphae memory and verifies its proofs, the Evaluator judges each claim against that evidence, and a fixed policy turns the result into a recommendation. Only a person can authorize it, and authorizing records a decision without executing anything.
App.buildNote: This build of the portal is not connected to the Hyphae Consensus API. It explains the system and shows the labels it will use; nothing in it calls a model or reads memory.

roles.title: Three roles deliberate
roles.body: The Proposer turns a task into explicit claims, the Critic challenges assumptions and risks, and the Proposer can revise.

evidence.title: The runtime checks evidence
evidence.body: The runtime, not a model, retrieves records from Hyphae memory and verifies their integrity proofs.

policy.title: A fixed policy recommends
policy.body: The Evidence Evaluator judges each claim against the evidence, and a deterministic policy turns those judgments and the proof statuses into a recommendation.

human.title: A person authorizes
human.body: Only a person can approve or reject. Approving records a decision; nothing is executed.

metricsPlanned.computed: show figures computed from the recorded runs themselves, never typed into the page;
metricsPlanned.labeled: label every figure with the runs, dates and policy version it comes from.

NewDeliberation.lead: Here you will start a deliberation in one of two modes.

planned.guided: offer a guided example that starts instantly, with scripted roles and simulated evidence, labeled SIMULATED and calling no model;
planned.live: offer the curated presets of the Live Meta mode, which call Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot (presets only, no free text; runs of the final recorded battery took about 4 to 7 minutes);
planned.fallback: offer a recorded run instead when live mode is busy or its daily budget is used up;
planned.return: let you leave and come back to your run through My runs.

Runs.count: {count, plural, =0 {No runs yet} one {# run} other {# runs}}

planned.own: list only the runs started in this browser session; there is no list of other visitors’ runs;
planned.expiry: keep each run reachable for 24 hours and delete its files after 7 days;
planned.status: show whether a run is still deliberating, awaiting your decision or finished.

Showcase.lead: Real runs recorded on 26 and 27 October 2026, to be replayed from a verbatim archive.

planned.recorded: replay each run from the archive, labeled RECORDED; a replay is never presented as a live run;
planned.corrections: show the dated corrections that apply to each run;
planned.manifest: link each run to its archived log, whose SHA-256 is pinned in the archive’s manifest.

Tour.inviteTitle: New here? Take the one-minute tour
Tour.inviteText: Six short steps through the main ideas. You can skip it at any time and open it again from Docs.

welcome.title: Welcome to Hyphae Consensus
welcome.body: Three AI roles work through a software-engineering problem, the runtime checks the evidence, and a fixed policy recommends. Only a person can authorize. In this build the portal is not connected, so its views say what they will do.

guided.title: Start with a guided example
guided.body: Once the portal is connected, a guided example will start instantly. Its roles will be scripted and its evidence simulated, so it will be labeled SIMULATED and will call no model.

live.title: Live Meta presets
live.body: Live runs will call Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 on curated presets, with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot. Runs of the final recorded battery took about 4 to 7 minutes. When live mode is busy or its daily budget is used up, a recorded run will be offered instead.

runs.title: Come back through My runs
runs.body: A run will keep going if you close the page. You will find it again in My runs, where each run stays reachable for 24 hours.

labels.title: Read the labels
labels.body: Every run and event will say where it comes from: SIMULATED, LIVE META next to its evidence label, RECORDED or REPLAY. A valid proof shows that Hyphae can reproduce the sealed recall a record came from, not that the record is true.

decide.title: You decide, and nothing executes
decide.body: The recommendation comes from a deterministic policy, not from a vote. Approving records your decision only: no executor exists, and decisions made in the public portal carry no authority.

Provenance.heading: Provenance labels
Provenance.intro: Once connected, the portal will mark every run and event with where it comes from, on separate axes: the model (scripted or live Meta), the evidence (simulated or a sealed snapshot), the source (this server or the research archive) and the delivery of each event (live or replay). Labels will come from recorded data, never from the request. What they will mean:

simulated.label: SIMULATED
simulated.description: Simulated evidence: its proofs are not real. In guided runs the roles are scripted too and no model is called.

liveMeta.label: LIVE META
liveMeta.description: A run in progress: live calls to Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0, with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot whose proofs are re-verified for every run. LIVE META never stands alone; the evidence label is always next to it.

hybrid.description: A live model with simulated evidence: real model calls, but proofs that are not real. Some runs in the research archive are of this kind, and their labels say so.

recorded.label: RECORDED
recorded.description: A real run recorded earlier and shown from the research archive, not a run in progress. It keeps the model and evidence labels it was recorded with.

replay.label: REPLAY
replay.description: Stored events played back, not as they happen. A recorded run always plays as a replay.

Provenance.note: A valid proof shows that Hyphae can reproduce the sealed recall a record came from, not that the record is true, relevant or complete, or that a model used it.
